name: Claymation
definition: A 30 second stop-motion comedy on a handmade miniature set: plasticine characters with visible thumbprints and tool marks, cardboard and painted-wood buildings, cotton-wool clouds, animated on twos at 12 fps so every frame feels touched by a hand. The product is a real object standing on the set, a giant landmark to the tiny characters.
why_it_sells: Handmade texture reads as craft and care, the opposite of a polished ad, so it stops the scroll: creators report claymation CTR at 2 to 3x the feed average and it is winning in multiple Meta accounts. It is also the family of 'material' looks (felt, crochet, LEGO) that practitioners use as a variety lever on the same script, so one board yields several fresh creatives.
visual_grammar: Miniature scale that is proud of itself: shallow depth of field like a macro lens on a tabletop, characters 3 to 5 cm tall, props from real life at real size (a bottle cap is a podium, a drainpipe is a highway). Chunky simple character shapes, bead or button eyes with painted highlights, mouths as replaceable clay shapes. Visible fingerprints, slight lumpiness, a seam here and there. Sets are flat-painted cardboard, balsa and felt, lit like a tabletop. The product is the only thing on the set that is not handmade, which makes it the hero by contrast.
camera: Tabletop camera: locked off most of the time (stop-motion rarely moves), slow motion-control slides or push-ins for hero beats, low macro angles at character height so the set feels huge. No handheld. Crash zooms are done as 3 or 4 hard stepped frames, not smooth.
light: Warm tabletop key from one side (a studio softbox look), bounce fill, a small back light that shows fuzz on felt and the clay's matte surface. Light is steady; the only flicker allowed is the faint frame-to-frame exposure breathing of real stop-motion.
texture: Matte plasticine with thumbprints, tool marks and tiny dust specks, felt and card surfaces with fibres, painted wood grain, cotton-wool clouds on wires. Slight frame-to-frame 'boil' in the clay surfaces. Motion blur is faked with clay smears, never real camera blur.
palette_rule: Build the set from saturated, slightly chalky craft colours with the product's colours as the town's colours (here: sky-blue and silver cardboard buildings, red and gold accents), so the real can looks like it belongs to the town while its printed metal still pops against matte clay.
pacing: Hook: a funny character and a line in the first 2 s. Shots of 2 to 4 s held longer than live action because the audience savours the craft. Comic beats land on a held pose of 6 to 8 frames. Product beat held at least 2 s. The fastest section uses stepped clay smears and hard cuts on twos.
sound: Native sound from the generations, recorded close and a little dry: squelchy clay footsteps, wooden clacks, cardboard rattles, voices with character. One jaunty score (plucked banjo or ukulele, woodblock, clarinet, brushed snare) stitched across units. Added sound only for events the viewer must register (the can crack, the starter pop).

caption_look.shadow: hard 0 4px 0 #3B2A1E offset (a cut-paper drop shadow), no blur
caption_look.position: centre, 69% down the frame, clear of the platform UI safe zone
caption_look.motion: captions animate on twos (12 fps) with a 1 px random jitter per frame so the type boils like the clay

model_vocab: tabletop macro lens, shallow depth of field
animated on twos at 12 frames per second

variants.felt: Feltmation: needle-felted wool characters with fuzzy halos under back light, felt and fabric sets, yarn details; everything softer and warmer; same timing on twos.
variants.crochet: Crochet: characters and sets knitted and crocheted in chunky yarn with visible stitches, amigurumi proportions, safety-eye plastic eyes; suits cosy, home and baby-free lifestyle products.
variants.lego: Brick build: characters are generic unbranded minifigure-like figures and every set is built from generic interlocking plastic bricks with studs; never show a real toy brand's logo on studs; stepped stop-motion at 12 fps; good for playful tech and gaming products.

product_integration: Decision: the REAL can stands on the clay set, not a clay-sculpted can. Reasons: (1) a sculpted can forces the model to redraw the wordmark, bulls and SUGARFREE in clay, which is exactly where image and video models garble text; (2) real stop-motion commercials put the genuine product on the miniature set all the time, so it reads as authentic, not as a compositing error; (3) printed aluminium against matte plasticine is the strongest possible contrast, so the product is the hero of every frame it is in. Rules: the can is at true scale (the characters are 3 to 5 cm tall, so the can is a tower to them), lit by the same warm tabletop key, casting a soft contact shadow on the set; clay props may touch it (a clay straw, a clay hand) but never cover the front label.
failure_modes: the model sculpts the can in clay and garbles the wordmark: always say 'the exact real can from the product reference, a real printed aluminium can standing on the miniature clay set, not made of clay'
the characters go smooth and CG (no thumbprints) and the look slides into 3D animation: say 'visible thumbprints, matte plasticine, handmade' every time
the snail's shell spiral, cap colour or satchel swap between shots: pass the cast card and restate cap and satchel colours
scale drifts so the can shrinks to character size: state 'the can towers over him like a building' in every can shot
banners, mailboxes and post-office signs grow fake lettering: say 'blank banners, plain signs with no letters'
smooth video-model motion kills the stop-motion feel: the video prompt must say 'stop-motion animation on twos at 12 fps, slight frame-to-frame clay boil, no motion blur'
wide street scenes in 9:16 come back rotated: say 'upright vertical composition, level horizon, the table surface flat'
the rival's roller skates or bike wheels float off the ground: say 'wheels on the ground, normal gravity'
a character who speaks in the hook gets staged tiny in a wide establishing frame: say 'fills the upper two thirds of the frame, close to the lens' so the hook reads on a phone
in busy multi-character shots the hero's clay colours drift (Gus came back bright green): restate body and shell colours and add 'not bright green' style exclusions
the real can's pull tab comes back blue or silver instead of red: minor, fix in the video unit by referencing the official can

the model gives the snail arms and inflates him to rabbit size when he has to do something with his hands: say 'no arms, a snail's body only', have him act with his head or eyestalks, and state the relative heights of the cast
race starts drift to starter pistols, which read as a gun in feed: use a starter's flag and say no guns or weapons
negatives: no real brands, logos or signage except the product
no readable text generated by the model anywhere in frame
no clay-sculpted or cartoon version of the product
no smooth CG surfaces, no photoreal animals
no guns or weapons, including toy or starter pistols
prompt_prefix: Claymation stop-motion still, vertical 9:16 frame, handmade miniature set of cardboard, balsa and felt, plasticine characters with visible thumbprints and tool marks, matte clay, warm tabletop softbox key light, macro lens with shallow depth of field.
asset_style: Rendered as a handmade claymation stop-motion puppet: matte plasticine with visible thumbprints and tool marks, bead eyes with painted highlights, photographed on a tabletop with a warm softbox.
